marks.gloss_en: מנין... דכתיב ואשר הרעתי
as it is written: 'and whom I have wronged' (Micah 4:6)
הא אשר אמרתי -- אשר אמרת מיבעי ליה! Moses is recalling God's promise to the forefathers, so the verse should say 'of which You have spoken'
Moses's prayer: 'and You said to them: I will multiply your seed as the stars of heaven, and all this land of which I have spoken...' (Ex 32:13)
עד כאן דברי תלמיד, מכאן ואילך דברי הרב -- the clause is God's own words, so 'I' is right (= p_divrei_harav)
אלו ואלו דברי תלמיד -- Moses speaks throughout: what You told me to say in Your name I said -- now what shall I say to them? (= p_divrei_talmid, p_ma_ani_omer_lahem)
R' Elazar: up to here the words of the student; from here on the words of the Master -- 'of which I have spoken' is God speaking
were the verse not written, it would be impossible to say it
ומה כסא של שלש רגלים אינו יכול לעמוד לפניך בשעת כעסך, כסא של רגל אחד על אחת כמה וכמה -- a three-legged chair cannot stand before God's anger; a one-legged chair a fortiori cannot
Moses: Master of the world, if a chair of three legs cannot stand before You in the hour of Your anger, a chair of one leg all the more so
Moses: moreover, I have shame before my fathers -- now they will say: see the leader He set over them; he sought greatness for himself and did not seek mercy for them
what is 'go, descend' (Ex 32:7)? R' Elazar: the Holy One said to Moses: Moses, descend from your greatness

a parable: a king angry at his son beat him severely; his friend sat before him, afraid to speak. The king said: were it not for this friend of mine before me, I would have killed you. [The friend] said: this matter depends on me -- and at once stood and rescued him
מבלתי יכלת ה' -- יכול ה' מיבעי ליה! the verse should have used the verb 'was able' (yachol), not the noun 'ability' (yecholet)
Moses's prayer: [the nations will say] 'because the Lord was without the ability (yecholet) to bring this people into the land' (Num 14:16)
אמר משה לפני הקדוש ברוך הוא: עכשיו יאמרו אומות העולם תשש כחו כנקבה -- the feminine form voices what the nations will say, that His strength waned like a female's (= p_tashash_kocho)
Moses: Master of the world, now the nations of the world will say: His strength has waned like a female's and He cannot save
R' Yochanan: the Holy One went back and conceded to Moses
happy is the student whose master concedes to him
Rav Yitzchak: 'but as I live' (Num 14:21) teaches that the Holy One said to Moses: Moses, you have given Me life with your words
had it not been for these three verses, the feet of 'the enemies of Israel' (a euphemism for Israel) would have collapsed

the three: 'and those whom I have dealt with wickedly' (Micah 4:6); 'behold, as clay in the potter's hand, so are you in My hand, house of Israel' (Jer 18:6); 'and I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh' (Ezek 36:26)
Rav Pappa: from here -- 'and I will put My spirit within you and cause you to walk in My statutes' (Ezek 36:27)
Moses spoke impertinently toward Heaven
the school of R' Eliezer b. Yaakov read alef as ayin and ayin as alef
the school of R' Yannai: [that Moses spoke impertinently is] from here -- 'and Di Zahav' (Deut 1:1)
what is 'Di Zahav'? the school of R' Yannai: it is what Moses said before the Holy One -- 'enough (dai) gold'
a lion does not roar over a basket of straw but over a basket of meat
R' Oshaya: a parable -- a man had a lean, large-limbed cow; he fed it lupines and it kicked him. He said: who caused you to kick me, if not the lupines I fed you?
R' Yochanan: a parable -- a man bathed and anointed his son, fed him and gave him drink, hung a purse on his neck and set him at the door of a brothel: what can that son do not to sin?
that is what people say: a full belly is a kind of evil
and if you wish, say from here: 'and Jeshurun grew fat and kicked' (Deut 32:15)
a person should always set out the praise of the Holy One and afterwards pray
כתיב הכא ויחל, וכתיב התם לא יחל דברו, ואמר מר: הוא אינו מיחל אבל אחרים מחלין לו -- vayechal here is the annulment of a vow, as lo yachel there
R' Elazar: 'and Moses besought (vayechal) the Lord' teaches that Moses stood in prayer before the Holy One until it made him ill
Shmuel: it teaches that he gave himself over to death for them
Rav Yitzchak: it teaches that he caused the attribute of mercy to rest upon them
the Rabbis: it teaches that Moses said before the Holy One: Master of the world, it is a profanation for You to do such a thing
R' Eliezer HaGadol: it teaches that Moses stood in prayer before the Holy One until achilu seized him

Moses: had You sworn to them by heaven and earth, I would say that as heaven and earth pass away so does Your oath; now that You swore to them by Your great name, as Your great name lives and endures forever, so Your oath endures forever
